description: WindGym is a DTU Wind Energy Systems package for developing reinforcement-learning controllers for wind farms. It connects single-agent or multi-agent policies to wind-farm dynamics represented through DYNAMIKS and PyWake. The documentation describes turbine yaw control, power maximization and load reduction, with configurable turbulence, turbine models, measurement noise and baseline agents. Wind conditions, turbine layout and episode duration define each experiment, so the software has no fixed geographical footprint or historical coverage. Python interfaces follow Gymnasium and PettingZoo, with installation instructions and notebooks available from the public repository. Source code is free under MIT. A modeller can compare control strategies and their sensitivity to uncertain observations before considering operational deployment. A limitation is that conclusions depend on the selected flow-model fidelity and turbine representation. Some documented high-fidelity turbine options require additional software. No directly related existing catalogue record was established for WindGym. The review checked repository metadata and documentation without training agents or running wind-farm simulations.
